source.title: A Geometric Account of Activation Steering through Angle-Norm Decomposition

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or truncation; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures angular versus radial encoding of selected concepts and steering stability in LLMs, but does not test sparse-feature superposition, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE feature recovery, or the dimensionality of superposed features.
record.gate_note: The paper reports probe accuracies for raw, unit-normalized, and norm-only activations. These bear on concept encoding but do not measure the superposition, feature overlap, neuron polysemanticity, or feature dimensionality named by the claim versions; they are recorded as findings fitting no version. Steering and norm-scaling results concern intervention stability, not the claim versions, and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares activation-steering geometry (angle vs. norm) in seven LLMs. Its probe results show that four selected concepts are linearly decodable from unit-normalized activations but not from the norm. It never measures feature superposition, overlap or interference, neuron polysemanticity, SAE features, or feature dimensionality, and it does not cite the Toy Models paper. The only point of contact is a speculative remark that the norm partly controls 'representational capacity' at a token, which is untested. 'discusses' is a loose fit; the paper barely touches the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find the evaluated concepts encoded mainly in activation direction, with norm governing steering stability and capability retention. They propose treating steering as a two-parameter (angle, radius) intervention.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses contrastive mean-difference directions and inference-time angular/radial edits in pretrained LLM residual streams; it does not train toy networks with sparse features or measure feature overlap and interference.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported norm and steering outcomes vary with model architecture, layer, steering strength, target angular score, and norm scale; the authors apply steering at one layer per model, chosen at 75% depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 7 LLMs and 4 concept datasets, probes on unit-normalized activations match raw-activation probes, while norm-only probes sit near chance (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept information for truthfulness, sentiment and toxicity in LLM residual streams is carried by activation direction, not magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: With the angular concept score fixed, scaling the norm by β=1.2 instead of 1.0 cuts the perplexity ratio from 151.8 to 83.5 at γ=0.7. The task metric spread stays at or below 2.5pp (Tables 7–8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hidden-state norm acts as a stability parameter under strong steering, possibly reflecting per-token representational capacity (authors' hypothesis, untested).

record.problems: The authors note that steering is tested at a single fixed layer per model, the model and concept set is limited, all methods use the same contrastive mean-difference direction, and the norm-scale sweep uses only a small discrete set of β values. Results are aggregated using one seed and two folds; probe-table uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on the listed claim versions were omitted. Steering-performance, perplexity, MMLU, and norm-variation results were left out because they do not measure the superposition or feature properties named in the versions.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweeps, or feature-overlap geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity-allocation measurement; the norm-as-capacity idea is only a hypothesis.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons.
No measure of features spread across neurons and no SAE recovery; probes use dense contrastive mean-difference directions.
Single mean-difference directions are assumed for steering; their dimensionality versus multi-dimensional features is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The probe rows are correctly linked to 'none'. Gemma-2-9B-it raw probes are weak (e.g., TruthfulQA 57.6%), so for Gemma, 'unit matches raw' tells little. The steering, perplexity and MMLU results were reasonably left out, since they concern the intervention rather than the claim.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, sparse-feature counts, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular feature geometry are tested.
No neuron polysemanticity or competition between features for dedicated versus shared dimensions is measured.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are tested.
The paper does not measure feature distribution across neurons or recover sparse features with an SAE.
No SAE features or claims about their completeness, stability, or canonical status are evaluated.
The paper does not test whether features involved in superposition are one-dimensional or multidimensional.
